text.p: Italy's largest quoted retailer Rinascente and French privately-owned retail group Auchan agreed on Tuesday to pool their Italian operations to form new powerful force in Italian retailing.

The Italian group which owns the Rinascente chain, UPIM stores, Citta Mercato hypermarkets and Bricocenter home improvement outlets is joining together with Auchan's four Italian hypermarkets and its property and service operations.

In a complex deal, the Agnelli family holding IFIL, which currently controls Rinascente, said it is looking to create a long term partnership with one of Europe's leading retailers to capitalise on the Rinascente name.

In the operation, IFIL's 92.7 percent-owned holding Eufin will contribute its 40.5 percent Rinascente stake to the IFIL-Auchan grouping. Then after Rinascente has completed a 780 billion lire ($457 million) capital increase the new grouping will be owned 51 percent by IFIL and 49 percent by Auchan.

The capital increase will allow Rinascente to buy Auchan's interests in Italy for 530 billion lire, and then see Auchan contribute to the capital increase, thus allowing the French company entry to the new grouping.
"We know the qualities of Rinascente, by joining forces and capabilities, will guarantee our future success," said Auchan chairman Gerard Mulliez.
IFIL's chairman Umberto Agnelli said the new grouping would exploit the great potential of Rinascente and offer opportunities to Italian and French producers.
Italian stock market watchdog Consob said it had allowed Auchan to take the stake in Rinascente without the obligation to bid for the remaining shares.
After ten years finishing on January 1, 2007, Auchan will have the right to increase its shareholding in the new group to make the new company a 50-50 percent Italian-French venture.
The statement said that after 15 years, IFIL will have the possibility of continuing the association or reducing its stake -- either partially or totally.
In the deal, IFIL was advised by Mediobanca and Auchan by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Auchan's Italian operations are expected to have 900 billion lire of sales in 1997, after some 800 billion lire in 1996, and 2,000 employees. Rinascente expects to have sales of eight trillion lire in 1997 including Auchan's Italian interests.
IFIL shares closed up 4.32 percent at 5,173 lire in a firmer Milan stock market but Rinascente shares were suspended for the day pending the Auchan announcement.
